headline: Medium-risk pair: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways; no direct evidence of tighter isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT exposes a filesystem and shell, while RD-Agent reads/writes logs and uses APIs; that creates a plausible content-bridging path where one agent can feed the other untrusted instructions through shared files or outputs. No direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or log directory, injected instructions can traverse between them.
IF either agent parses file contents as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and log directories per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files.
Review any shared prompts before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem ACLs between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and make allowlisted network calls; RD-Agent handles sensitive classes like financial reports, execution traces, and logs and sends data to external APIs. If they share a workspace, either agent can expose the other's files or derived context to third parties, so the default blast radius includes sensitive work products.
conditions: IF the two agents share a directory containing reports, logs, or datasets, those contents can be exposed through either agent's API calls.
IF AutoGPT is given sensitive files from RD-Agent, its allowlisted egress can still transmit derived content externally.
mitigations: Use separate storage roots for each agent.
Keep sensitive datasets out of shared folders.
Restrict outbound API destinations for both agents.
Rotate or redact logs before either agent reads them.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on inter-agent file transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and RD-Agent supports multiple instances with API/file activity. Even without explicit shared-write proof, overlapping mutable filesystem and process activity can collide on shared resources; uncertainty about orchestration and locking warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout, file races and overwrite conflicts can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared API-backed state without locks, concurrent updates can diverge.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Avoid concurrent git operations in the same repo.
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate shell-driven outputs and RD-Agent is a research automation system that consumes files, logs, and API results. If RD-Agent treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research artifacts or actions. The pair lacks documented verification barriers, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests AutoGPT-produced text without verification, incorrect facts can propagate into reports or code.
IF AutoGPT writes malformed artifacts that RD-Agent later executes or summarizes, the error chain widens.
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions.
Add checksum or schema validation between agents.
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted by default.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only consumption of peer outputs.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly touches financial reports, execution traces, logs, and competition datasets, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and external egress. That combination creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated data is placed in shared storage. No specific jurisdictional controls are documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in a shared workspace, retention and access controls must cover both agents.
IF either agent sends logs or reports to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Redact logs before external transmission.
Document retention periods for each agent.
Restrict secrets to the minimum needed.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
